text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigerian appeal court turns down request from lawyer of detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola to visit him. Abiola claims victory in a 1993 presidential election which was annulled by the military.
- Vehicles in the northern city of Kaduna are to be allowed to buy only 300 naira worth of fuel at a time, to ensure fair distribution during a local fuel crisis.
- Production of cement at the Cement Company of Northern Nigeria may stop following large financial losses and a dwindling demand for products.
- British Airways officials are optimistic that an end may soon be found to the row between Britain and Nigeria which has stopped flights between the two countries.
- Nigerian Postal Services has begun to phase out manual franking machines in favour of a computerised method.
- Eastern community demands compensation of 25 million naira from Imo Rubber Estate for encroaching on local farm land.

- Outgoing managing director of Royal Dutch/Shell's Nigeria unit, Brian Anderson, says government should fund the oil industry effectively by either providing more money or divesting from its 57 percent stake in joint ventures.
- Four major cities in the United States have imposed trade embargoes on Nigeria.
